sandbox: macOS sandbox-exec: no network, home folder unreadable, one scratch folder writable

tools.name: specifier_set_to_range
tools.description: Convert a specifier set to a version range that represents the same versions. specifiers: A string representation of version specifiers, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0' -> '[1.0, 2.0.dev0)'.

tools.name: filter_specifier_set
tools.description:
Filter an iterable of items to only include those that match all specifiers in this set.
    
    :param specifiers: A string containing version specifiers (e.g., '>=1.2.3')
    :param iterable: An iterable of version strings or Version instances to filter
    :param prereleases: Whether to include prereleases; if None, follows PEP 440 recommendation
    :return: List of items that match all specifiers
    
    >>> filter_specifier_set(">=1.2.3", ["1.2", "1.3", "1.5a1"])
    ['1.3']

tools.name: create_full_version_range
tools.description: Return the full range that includes all possible PEP 440 versions. admit_arbitrary: whether to admit arbitrary version strings; prereleases: whether to include pre-release versions. Example: create_full_version_range() -> "<VersionRange object>"

tools.name: filter_version_range
tools.description:
Yield items from iterable whose version falls inside the range.
    
    Args:
        specifiers: A string representing version specifiers (e.g., '>=1.0,<2.0')
        iterable: An iterable of version strings
        prereleases: Whether to include pre-releases; None uses PEP 440 default behavior
    
    Example:
        >>> filter_version_range(">=1.0,<2.0", ["0.9", "1.5", "2.0"])
        ['1.5']

tools.name: check_unsatisfiable_specifier_set
tools.description:
Check whether this specifier set can never be satisfied.
    
    A specifier set is unsatisfiable if no version can satisfy all specifiers simultaneously.
    
    Args:
        specifiers (str): A string representation of version specifiers
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if no version can satisfy all specifiers simultaneously
        
    Example:
        >>> check_unsatisfiable_specifier_set(">=2.0,<1.0")
        True

tools.name: check_prerelease_version
tools.description: Determine if a version is a pre-release version. version: A version string to check if it is a pre-release version -> true if pre-release, false otherwise.

tools.name: check_specifier_contains
tools.description: Check if a specific version is contained within a specifier. specifier: A version specifier string, e.g., '>=1.2.3'. version: The version string to check against the specifier. prereleases: Whether or not to match prereleases with this Specifier. If None, follows PEP 440 defaults. >>> check_specifier_contains('>=1.2.3', '1.2.3') True

tools.name: filter_specifier
tools.description:
Filter items in the given iterable, that match the specifier.
    
    Args:
        specifier: A version specifier string
        iterable: An iterable of version strings and/or Version instances
        prereleases: Whether or not to allow prereleases in the returned iterator
        
    Returns:
        List of items from iterable that match the specifier
        
    Example:
        >>> filter_specifier(">=1.2.3", ["1.2", "1.3", "1.5a1"])
        ['1.3']

tools.name: check_specifier_set_contains
tools.description: Check if a specific version is contained within a specifier set. specifier_set: A string representation of the specifier set (e.g., '>=1.0.0,!=1.0.1'), version: The version string to check for containment in the specifier set, prereleases: Whether or not to match prereleases with this SpecifierSet. If set to None (the default), it will follow the recommendation from PEP 440. >>> check_specifier_set_contains('>=1.0.0,!=1.0.1', '1.2.3') True

tools.name: create_empty_version_range
tools.description: Create an empty version range that contains no versions. prereleases: whether prereleases should be considered when checking version inclusion -> the empty version range

tools.name: create_singleton_version_range
tools.description: Return the strict singleton range `{version}` as a string representation. version: A PEP 440 compliant version string, e.g. '1.0' -> '{1.0}'. prereleases: Whether to include pre-release versions.

tools.name: canonicalize_version
tools.description: Return a canonical form of a version as a string. version: A version string to canonicalize, e.g. '1.0.0' -> '1'. strip_trailing_zero: Whether to strip trailing zeros from the release segment, e.g. '1.0.0' with strip_trailing_zero=False -> '1.0.0'.

tools.name: get_pre_release_segment
tools.description: Get the pre-release segment of a version. version: A version string to parse -> The pre-release segment as (type, number) or None.

tools.name: get_version_range_complement
tools.description:
Get the complement of a version range, containing all versions not in the original range.
    
    Args:
        version_range (str): A version range specifier compatible with packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet
        
    Returns:
        str: The complement version range as a string
        
    Example:
        >>> get_version_range_complement(">=1.0")
        '<1.0'

tools.name: check_version_range_subset
tools.description: Check if every version in range1 is also in range2. range1: first version range specifier, range2: second version range specifier to check against. >>> check_version_range_subset('>=1.5,<1.8', '>=1.0,<2.0') -> True

tools.name: canonicalize_package_name
tools.description: Normalize a package name to its canonical form. name: The package name to normalize. validate: Check whether the name is a valid distribution name. >>> canonicalize_package_name("Django") 'django'

tools.name: get_release_components
tools.description:
Get the release components of a version. version: A version string to parse and extract release components from
    
    >>> get_release_components("1.2.3")
    [1, 2, 3]
    >>> get_release_components("2.0.0")
    [2, 0, 0]
    >>> get_release_components("1!2.0.0.post0")
    [2, 0, 0]

tools.name: get_post_release_number
tools.description:
Get the post-release number of a version. version: A version string to parse and extract the post-release number from
    
    >>> print(get_post_release_number("1.2.3"))
    None
    >>> get_post_release_number("1.2.3.post1")
    1

tools.name: check_post_release_version
tools.description: Determine if a version is a post-release version. version: A version string to check if it is a post-release version -> true if post-release, false otherwise.

tools.name: difference_version_ranges
tools.description:
Get the difference between two version ranges, including versions in the first but not the second.
    
    Args:
        first_range (string): The first version range specifier
        second_range (string): The second version range specifier to subtract from the first
        
    Returns:
        string: A string representation of the resulting version range
        
    Example:
        >>> difference_version_ranges(">=1.0", ">=2.0")
        '>=1.0,<2.0'

tools.name: check_disjoint_version_ranges
tools.description:
Check if two version ranges have no overlapping versions.
    
    Args:
        version_range1 (str): First version range specifier (e.g., '>=1.0,<2.0')
        version_range2 (str): Second version range specifier (e.g., '>=2.0,<3.0')
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if the ranges are disjoint (no overlap), False otherwise
        
    Example:
        >>> check_disjoint_version_ranges('>=1.0,<2.0', '>=2.0,<3.0')
        True

tools.name: check_specifier_set_subset
tools.description:
Check if every version matching this set also matches another set.
    
    Args:
        specifier_set: The specifier set to check if it is a subset of the other set
        other_set: The specifier set to check against
    
    Returns:
        True if every version matching specifier_set also matches other_set, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> check_specifier_set_subset(">=3.12,<3.13", ">=3.12")
        True

tools.name: check_disjoint_specifier_sets
tools.description:
Check if two specifier sets have no matching versions.
    
    Args:
        specifiers1 (str): A string of version specifiers for the first set
        specifiers2 (str): A string of version specifiers for the second set
    
    Returns:
        bool: True if the sets have no matching versions, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> check_disjoint_specifier_sets("<3.12", ">=3.12")
        True

tools.name: validate_normalized_name
tools.description: Check if a name is already in its normalized form. name: The project name to check for normalization -> true if the name is normalized, false otherwise.

tools.name: normalize_pre_release_segment
tools.description: Normalize the pre-release segment of a version string. letter: The pre-release segment to normalize, e.g. 'alpha' -> 'a'.

tools.name: get_epoch_component
tools.description:
Get the epoch component of a version. version: A version string compatible with packaging.version.Version -> The epoch of the version.
    
    >>> get_epoch_component("2.0.0")
    0
    >>> get_epoch_component("1!2.0.0")
    1

tools.name: get_public_version
tools.description: Get the public portion of a version string. version: A version string to extract the public portion from -> The public portion without local version identifiers.

tools.name: get_base_version
tools.description: Get the base version of a version string. version: A version string to extract the base version from -> '1.2.3'.

tools.name: evaluate_marker
tools.description: Evaluate a marker expression against an environment. marker: A marker expression to evaluate, e.g. 'python_version >= "3.6"' -> True. environment: Mapping containing keys and values to override the detected environment. context: The context in which the marker is evaluated, which influences what marker names are considered valid. Accepted values are "metadata" (default), "lock_file", and "requirement".

tools.name: check_version_range_superset
tools.description: Check if every version in another range is also in this range. range1: A version range specifier string, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0'. range2: Another version range specifier string to check if it's a subset of range1. Example: check_version_range_superset('>=1.0,<2.0', '>=1.5,<1.8') -> True.

tools.name: check_version_range_contains
tools.description:
Check if a specific version is contained within a version range.
    
    Args:
        version_range: A version range specifier compatible with packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet
        version: The version string to check against the range
    
    Returns:
        bool: True if the version is contained in the range, False otherwise
    
    Example:
        >>> check_version_range_contains(">=1.0,<2.0", "1.5")
        True

tools.name: check_specifier_set_superset
tools.description:
Return whether every version matching other also matches this set.
    
    Args:
        specifier_set (str): The specifier set to check against
        other_set (str): The other specifier set to compare with
    
    Returns:
        bool: True if every version matching other also matches this set
    
    Example:
        >>> check_specifier_set_superset(">=3.12", ">=3.12,<3.13")
        True

tools.name: parse_version_string
tools.description:
Parse the given version string.
    
    This is identical to the Version constructor.
    
    >>> parse_version_string('1.0.dev1')
    '1.0.dev1'
    
    :param version: The version string to parse.
    :raises ValueError: When the version string is not a valid version.

tools.name: get_dev_release_number
tools.description: Get the development release number of a version. version: A version string to parse and extract the development release number from -> The development number of the version, or None if not a development version.

tools.name: get_local_version_segment
tools.description: Get the local version segment of a version. version: A version string to parse, e.g. '1.2.3+abc' -> 'abc'.

tools.name: check_dev_release_version
tools.description: Determine if a version is a development release. version: A version string to check if it's a development release -> true if development release, false otherwise.

tools.name: get_minor_release_component
tools.description: Get the minor release component of a version. version: A version string to parse, e.g. '1.2.3' -> 2.

tools.name: get_micro_release_component
tools.description: Get the micro release component of a version. version: A version string to extract the micro release component from -> 3 for "1.2.3" or 0 if unavailable.

tools.name: get_major_release_component
tools.description: Get the major release component of a version. version: A version string to extract the major component from -> 1 for "1.2.3".
